findings.where: Page caption under every step (body line 101)
findings.what: The caption "Discharging turns both plates into lead sulphate and uses up acid. Charging runs it backwards." shows below the step 2, 4 and 8 puzzles and gives their answers before Check, so hide it until the finish panel, which already says the same thing.

findings.where: Step 5, Round the wire, last sentence
findings.what: "With both switches open, nothing flows and nothing changes" is absolute, because a real open cell slowly discharges itself and lesson 4's float exists to make up that loss, so say "almost nothing changes" or name self-discharge.

findings.where: Step 5, Round the wire, text against its finished picture
findings.what: The text ends on both switches open, but the finished picture and the read-through still show the lamp closed at 80% charge, so end on what the picture shows.

findings.where: Step 5, Round the wire, electron chevrons
findings.what: The chevrons run from the minus terminal through the lamp to the plus terminal, and no on-screen sentence says conventional current runs the other way; the explain says it, but an electrician reads arrows as conventional current, so add one short sentence here.
"Measured against the same reference" never says what the reference is or why it drops out of the gap, so one sentence comparing it to two voltages read from the same 0 V rail would close that step.

The "acid strength" heading and the "charge left 75%" readout share one line over one bar whose right end reads "charged", so the bar (at 83% when the charge is 75%) is easy to read as the charge left; move the readout or label the end "full strength".

findings.where: Lead paragraph above the stepper (body line 76)
findings.what: It repeats on all 13 steps and takes five lines at 360 px. It quotes "100 Ah at 1× plate size" before plate size comes up, and "which switches connect to a lamp or a charger" first reads as "which switches"; cut it to one plain sentence.

findings.where: Step 3, Charge running down, after a drag
findings.what: The text still says "Here the cell is at half charge" after Dan drags to, say, 75%, so tie that sentence to the end state ("At half charge, ...").

findings.where: Key inside the cell drawing, steps 3, 5 and 7
findings.what: Key entries pop in and jump around. "electron" appears without a fade when the lamp closes, and "lead sulphate" appears at the first drop in charge, pushing "ions" onto a second row; reserve their places or fade them in.
The key arrives at 0.5 s but the gauge above it only at 1.4 s, so the opening frame shows an empty band above a lone, faint "acid" key. Step 1's text also never says what the gauge is.

findings.where: Steps 2 and 8 after a right answer
findings.what: The electrons run for about 2 s and then freeze while the switch stays closed and the lamp stays lit (step 2 stops at 55%). Before Check the lamp is also lit with still electrons, so the picture shows a lit lamp with no current.

It asks what the plates turn into before any screen has named lead sulphate. It works as a prediction but is not framed as one, and its hint "Think about what each plate makes with the acid" points at nothing shown yet.
Only the two plates are named on the drawing. The terminals, the case and the electrolyte carry no label ("acid" appears only in the key), although the MCA asks him to draw and label the parts.

findings.where: Whole lesson (brief, lesson 1 row and syllabus list)
findings.what: The brief puts the difference between primary and secondary cells in lesson 1, because the MCA asks it, but no screen and not the explain names a secondary cell; one sentence on step 7 would cover it.
There are five footnote marks, and three of them ([^2], [^3] and a repeated [^4]) sit on how-it-works sentences rather than on a value he would look up, so keep [^1] on the 2.1 V and one [^4].
The charger has no + and − marks, so the picture never shows the charger's positive going to the cell's positive, the one connection an electrician must get right.
